prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood): auto start by demand/depth; permissives (suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips); lost permissive -> alarm/stop; maintenance release only after isolations tagged/verified/logged. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; uses Jar Test Photograph Set; adjusts within approved limits; shall hold last operator-approved dose if quality data bad. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt): staggers washes; shall provide reliable filter service status before demand counted as capacity. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note to Chief Operator; breakthrough -> offline until Chief Operator approves and rinse-to-waste meets target. Backwash Recovery Tank: receives spent washwater; returns after settling/clarity check, else hold. Chlorine Contact Basin: produces Chlorine Residual Alarm (pressure decisions then coordinated with water-quality response). Clearwell Level Controller: sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit; low-level interlock stops pumps; checked before large distribution adjustments. High Service Pump Header (Juniper): lead/lag, produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; reports pressure/flow/status. North and South Distribution Pressure Stations: auto mode sequences pumps within limits, reports abnormal starts/failures/valves; South starts lead booster on low pressure after delay; comm loss -> assume last confirmed mode. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow): sends Jar Test Photograph Set; records distribution samples (zone, point, time); provides analytical status. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern): uses Sample Chain Slip to link quality entries to log period; retains pressure/flow/pump/alarm data. Actors: Chief Operator (classifies upsets; produces Backwash Solids Manifest; may direct conservative pumping; closes upset); Duty Engineer (critical failures; reviews low-pressure complaints/alarms/model mismatch); Maintenance Planner (Quarry); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip); Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon; records reason/duration/contact for local/manual; sends Pressure Zone Handoff Card after verifying setpoints/alarms/field work; coordinates flushing/valve work); Field crews (notify before major valve operations); Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log); Residuals

New part:
S198: Control-room coordination with field crews is conducted by radio or phone using clear station names, valve identifiers, expected direction of pressure change, and confirmation when work is complete.
S199: Normal distribution operation is restored when pressure zones are stable, station alarms are cleared or assigned, field work is accounted for, and the Chief Operator has no remaining operating restrictions.
S200: The control system for the Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant shall use role-based access control with named accounts for operators, engineering users, maintenance users, and read-only review users.
S201: Shared credentials are not acceptable for routine operation of the River Intake Pump Station, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Coagulant Dosing Skid, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.
S202: Operator privileges shall be limited to the actions needed to run assigned plant areas, and engineering privileges shall require separate approval before setpoints, control logic, alarm limits, or historian configuration are changed.
S203: Remote access to the control network shall require multi-factor authentication, encrypted connectivity, a recorded business reason, and approval by the Chief Operator or Duty Engineer.
S204: Quarry maintains the weekly access review for maintenance accounts and disables privileges after reassignment.
S205: The SCADA Historian Server shall be protected as a critical asset because it supports compliance review, alarm analysis, operational trending, and event reconstruction.
S206: The control network shall be segmented from administrative networks, and only documented pathways shall be allowed between the SCADA Historian Server, operator workstations, controllers, and approved support systems.
S207: Security patches, firmware updates, and antivirus changes shall be tested in a controlled manner before deployment to equipment that affects water production or distribution pressure.
S208: The Chief Operator owns alarm governance for process alarms, and the Duty Engineer supports alarm limit review when control changes or recurring nuisance alarms are identified.
S209: Alarm priorities shall reflect consequence, response time, operator action, and the risk of losing treatment, storage, or distribution capability.
S210: A Chlorine Residual Alarm shall remain configured as a high-priority condition when residual concentration indicates a potential treatment compliance or public health concern.
S211: Alarm shelving, suppression, and disabling shall require a documented reason, a time limit, and review at the end of the operating shift.
S212: Standing alarms shall be reviewed during each shift turnover so that unresolved equipment failures are not hidden by routine acknowledgement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
